title: Iʿrāb in the Qur'an
hero_html:
COMBINED PRACTICE · QUR'AN

Iʿrāb in the Qur'an:
10 verses

Real verses with a past verb, a naṣb noun, and the rafʿ and jarr rules we already know. Same colours, same method.

القُرْآن

sections.title: Three small notes for these verses
sections.html:
Attached pronouns are fixed

ـهُ “his”, ـهَا “her”, ـكَ “your” join the noun before them. They are the owner, and fixed. We split them off so you can see the noun's ending: رَبَّـ | ـهُ.

A past verb can hide its doer

Like an order hides “you”, a past verb can hide “he” (هُوَ) or “she” (هِيَ). The ـتْ in قَدَّتْ tells us the doer is “she”.

Some names never take tanween

آدَمُ, سُلَيْمَانُ, دَاوُودَ: one damma or one fatha only. (Names like نُوحٌ do take it.)

Also: a past verb ending in ـتْ takes a small kasra before ال, just like an order verb: غَلَّقَتِ الأَبْوَابَ. It is still fixed.
